name: Cadmium arsenide
summary: A stable 3D Dirac semimetal with ultrahigh mobility. Its Dirac points are protected by C4 rotation symmetry.
caveats: Complex, partially ordered Cd-vacancy superstructure. Room-temperature structure refined as I41/acd. Many databases contain smaller P42/nmc approximants.

entries.title: The Crystal and Electronic Structures of Cd3As2, the Three-Dimensional Electronic Analogue of Graphene.

reference.title: The Crystal and Electronic Structures of Cd3As2, the Three-Dimensional Electronic Analogue of Graphene.

recommended_reason: Closest volume per atom to the experimental reference (COD 4337945) among DFT structures in the experimental space group.

description.text: Cd3As2 crystallizes in the tetragonal I4_1/acd space group. There are three inequivalent Cd sites. In the first Cd site, Cd(1) is bonded to one As(2), one As(3), and two equivalent As(1) atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing CdAs4 tetrahedra. The Cd(1)-As(2) bond length is 2.73 Å. The Cd(1)-As(3) bond length is 2.68 Å. There is one shorter (2.69 Å) and one longer (3.04 Å) Cd(1)-As(1) bond length. In the second Cd site, Cd(3) is bonded to one As(2), one As(3), and two equivalent As(1) atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing CdAs4 tetrahedra. The Cd(3)-As(2) bond length is 2.92 Å. The Cd(3)-As(3) bond length is 2.64 Å. There is one shorter (2.67 Å) and one longer (3.00 Å) Cd(3)-As(1) bond length. In the third Cd site, Cd(2) is bonded to one As(2), one As(3), and two equivalent As(1) atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing CdAs4 tetrahedra. The Cd(2)-As(2) bond length is 2.73 Å. The Cd(2)-As(3) bond length is 3.10 Å. There is one shorter (2.70 Å) and one longer (2.71 Å) Cd(2)-As(1) bond length. There are three inequivalent As sites. In the first As site, As(1) is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Cd(1), two equivalent Cd(2), and two equivalent Cd(3) atoms. In the second As site, As(2) is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Cd(1), two equivalent Cd(2), and two equivalent Cd(3) atoms. In the third As site, As(3) is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Cd(1), two equivalent Cd(2), and two equivalent Cd(3) atoms.

issues.text: Even the closest DFT structure differs from experiment by +5.8 % in volume per atom.
JARVIS-DFT has this composition only in other space groups (lowest energy: Pn-3m (No. 224)).
OQMD could not be reached when the data were fetched (2026-10-25).
There is no JARVIS-DFT entry in the experimental space group, so spin–orbit spillage, the mBJ gap and the BoltzTraP Seebeck coefficients are unavailable.
